'''Victor Nikolaevich Popov''' ({{langx|ru|Ви́ктор Никола́евич Попо́в}}; 27 October 1937 – 16 April 1994) was a [[Russians|Russian]] [[theoretical physicist]] known for his contribution to the quantization of non-abelian [[Gauge field theory|gauge fields]].  His work with [[Ludvig Faddeev]] on that subject introduced the fundamental objects now known as [[Faddeev–Popov ghost]]s.  

Popov graduated from the Department of Theoretical Physics of the Physics Faculty of [[Saint Petersburg State University|Leningrad State University]].  Popov formed a group at [[St. Petersburg Department of Steklov Mathematical Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences|Leningrad Department of Steklov Institute of Mathematics]] of the [[USSR Academy of Sciences]]  (LOMI) in early 1965, where he remained for life.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Faddeev |first1=L. D. |url=http://www.mathnet.ru/links/1b2affb553ca3061d262bad2fb2c7f1f/znsl4396.pdf |website=mathnet.ru|title=How I came to work with Victor Popov |publisher=All Russian mathematical portal}}</ref>
